chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Ammar Al-Dahhan, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the brothers of Yusuf threw Yusuf into the well, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to him and entered upon him and said: 'O boy, what are you doing here?' He said: 'My brothers threw me into the well.' He said: 'So would you like to be taken out from it?' He said: 'That is up to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If He wills, He will extract me.'

He said: So he said to him: 'Indeed Allah the Exalted is saying to you: Supplicate to Me with this supplication until I extract you from the well.' He said to him: 'And what is the supplication?' He said: 'Say:'

O Allah, I ask You by the fact that to You belongs all praise, there is no god except You, the Bestower, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Possessor of Majesty and Generosity, that You send Salat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You make for me a relief and an exit from what I am in.
He said: Then it was from his story what Allah mentioned in His Book.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication taught to Prophet Yusuf by Jibraeel for relief from distress?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Angel Jibraeel conveys a divine formula to Prophet Yusuf (AS) for deliverance from the well, establishing a foundational model for supplication in times of distress. The text highlights the Shia emphasis on invoking the Prophet and his Progeny (*Ahl al-Bayt*) as a means of seeking intercession and relief, linking Yusuf’s personal trial to the broader theological concept of divine mercy. This hadith is frequently cited in Shia devotional literature to demonstrate the efficacy of combining praise of Allah’s attributes with specific salutations upon the Prophet and his family.
